# Fact-check ledger

Cameron's manual-review queue from the editorial review
(sources/plan-review.md). One row per flag; written by the fact-check and
external-verification passes and by resolve-cites. **A row is a question,
not a verdict** — single-source ≠ wrong; nothing is deleted on the strength
of a flag. Categories: single-source | contradicted-by-source |
contradicted-internal | external-mismatch | cite-unresolved | unverifiable.
The external pass appends ` — verified-current <date> (<source>)` or
` — external-mismatch: …` to the detail cell of rows tagged `ext-verify`.

**Three sections, and only the first is a queue** (Cameron, 2026-08-26 —
"rest you can handle on your own"). The table between the markers holds the
rows that still need something from outside the corpus: each is tagged
`ext-verify` and is an input to `verify-external.yml`, the only workflow with
web access. Below the markers, **Standing** holds rows whose disposition the
KB's own rules already decide — the claim stands under flag, and the note
still carries that flag — and **Resolved** holds rows that are closed, with
how. Rows below the markers are invisible to the dashboard and to the
external verifier by design; they are the record, not the work.

Scotty (Brothers Sportfishing, the guest captain — not Roman Castro, whose channel this is) characterises the Coronados school as "a big old school" and gives school-size sufficiency as the mechanism — "if there's enough fish … the school is big enough there might be a fish that wants to eat it" — so smaller schools is a defensible inference, but it is an inference, and a reader taking "run smaller" as smaller FISH gets it backwards: he calls the coastal fish "these bigger grade fish". | locations/imperial-beach.md | slug-style plastics "with a top-hook configuration that will not foul on the bottom" | contradicted-by-source | `Kf5wk_TFgTc` | the source states the hook geometry comparatively, not absolutely: "you want something that has a top hook … like this this Hook is trailing out it gets very easily snagged so it's not [ideal]" (~07:24–07:32). A top hook is offered as the less snag-prone build, not as a build that will not foul. The note's absolute "will not foul on the bottom" is a hardening of a comparative, and it is the operative reason the note gives for the winter deep-structure build, so a reader takes it as a guarantee against a rock pipe. What the source does say about bottom contact is said of the trailing hook — "it's not something you want to bomb out and slow roll across the bottom … it's just going to get hooked up" — so the top hook is the build recommended FOR bottom work, which is why the hardening is easy to make and easy to miss. The slug preference itself verifies ("I prefer a slug style bait over a swimbait [because] it sinks faster"), as does the crankbait-over-suspended-bait half of the same sentence. The note's `asr-uncertain` note is accurate and, if anything, understated correctly — the BOAT NAME renders cleanly ("fishing on the city of Imperial Beach"); it is the departure point that is doubled and garbled ("out of I out of the pyramid Oh Beach"), which is exactly what the note says |

Adding `bay-harbor` to the flyline note's `waters` at its transform closes the gate half; a bay-harbor livebait bullet carrying `AH4Eiya1Hn0` closes the rest.
